problems.title: Black Swan and Tail Risk Robustness
problems.summary: Developing ML systems that can withstand rare, high-impact events (Black Swans) and long-tail risks, which current systems struggle with despite extensive training data, remains an open challenge.
problems.quote: Long-tail robustness is unusually challenging today and may become even more challenging. Long-tail robustness also requires more than human-level robustness; the 2008 financial crisis and COVID-19 have shown that even groups of humans have great difficulty mitigating and overcoming these rare but extraordinarily impactful long tail events.

problems.paper_title: Unsolved Problems in ML Safety
problems.section_title: 2.1 Black Swan and Tail Risk Robustness
problems.section_file: 2.1 Black Swan and Tail Risk Robustness.json
problems.title: Benchmarking Extreme Distribution Shifts
problems.summary: Creating benchmarks that stress-test ML systems with extreme, human-challenging distribution shifts and long-tail events, including artificial simulated data capturing structural properties of real-world tail risks, is needed.
problems.quote: Researchers could create more environments and benchmarks to stress-test systems, find their breaking points, and determine whether they will function appropriately in potential future scenarios. These benchmarks could include new, unusual, and extreme distribution shifts and long tail events, especially ones that are challenging even for humans.

problems.title: Unusual Data Sources for Robustness
problems.summary: Generating highly unusual but helpful data sources through new augmentation techniques or simulated data to improve ML system robustness to rare events is an open research direction.
problems.quote: The performance of many ML systems is currently largely shaped by data and parameter count, so future research could work on creating highly unusual but helpful data sources. The more experience a system has with unusual future situations, even ones not well represented in typical training data, the more robust it can be.

problems.paper_title: Unsolved Problems in ML Safety
problems.title: Broader Adversarial Robustness Definitions
problems.summary: Current research focuses on l-adversarial robustness with small p-norm constraints, but broader definitions are needed to address perceptible attacks or unknown attack specifications.
problems.quote: Current research largely focuses on the problem of 'l adversarial robustness,' [125, 30] where an adversary attempts to induce a misclassification but can only perturb inputs subject to a small p-norm constraint. While research on simplified problems helps drive progress, researchers may wish to avoid focusing too heavily on any one particular simplification.

problems.paper_title: Unsolved Problems in ML Safety
problems.title: Black-Box Adversarial Attacks
problems.summary: Defending against black-box attacks where adversaries have limited access to the ML system (e.g., zero-query or limited-query attacks) remains underexplored.
problems.quote: If a blackbox ML system is not publicly released and can only be queried, it may be possible to practically defend the system against zero-query attacks [189] or limited-query attacks [35].

problems.paper_title: Unsolved Problems in ML Safety
problems.title: Multi-Sensor Adversarial Defense
problems.summary: Exploiting information from multiple sensors (e.g., in autonomous vehicles) to detect inconsistencies in adversarial inputs is an underexplored defense approach.
problems.quote: Real world systems, such as autonomous vehicles, have multiple cameras. Researchers could exploit information from these different sensors and find inconsistencies in adversarial images in order to constrain and box in adversaries [202].

problems.paper_title: Unsolved Problems in ML Safety
problems.title: Adaptive Adversarial Defenses
problems.summary: Developing dynamic defenses that evolve during test time to counter adaptive adversaries is an open research direction.
problems.quote: Additionally, while existing ML defenses are typically static, future defenses could evolve during test time to combat adaptive adversaries [195].

problems.paper_title: Unsolved Problems in ML Safety
problems.title: Adversarially Robust Representations
problems.summary: Creating models with adversarially robust representations through data enhancement, architecture design, adversarial training improvements, and robustness certifications is an ongoing challenge.
problems.quote: Future research could do more work toward creating models with adversarially robust representations [41].

problems.paper_title: Unsolved Problems in ML Safety
problems.title: Unifying Adversarial and Long-Tail Robustness
problems.summary: Integrating adversarial robustness with robustness to long-tail or unusual events could improve systems' resilience to both worst-case scenarios.
problems.quote: It may also be possible to unify the areas of adversarial robustness and robustness to long-tail and unusual events.

problems.paper_title: Unsolved Problems in ML Safety
problems.title: Adversarial Anomaly Detection
problems.summary: Detecting adversarial anomalies or assigning them low confidence scores is a potential research direction for handling unusual adversarial inputs.
problems.quote: To study adversarial robustness on unusual inputs, researchers could also try detecting adversarial anomalies [17, 85] or assigning them low confidence [172].

problems.summary: Developing ML techniques to create effective defensive cybersecurity methods, such as detecting intruders, impersonators, and software vulnerabilities, and modeling software behavior to identify malicious activities.
problems.quote: To mitigate the potential harms of automated cyberattacks to ML and other systems, researchers should apply ML to develop better defensive techniques.

problems.paper_title: Unsolved Problems in ML Safety
problems.title: ML for Malicious Payload Detection
problems.summary: Using unsupervised ML methods to model binaries and detect obfuscated malicious payloads in software.
problems.quote: Massive unsupervised ML methods could also model binaries and learn to detect malicious obfuscated payloads [168, 161, 134, 71].

problems.paper_title: Unsolved Problems in ML Safety
problems.title: ML for Automated Security Patching
problems.summary: Advancing code translation and generation models to automatically apply security patches and improve code security.
problems.quote: Advancements in code translation [111, 9] and code generation [34, 138] suggest that future models could apply security patches and make code more secure, so that future systems not only flag security vulnerabilities but also fix them.

problems.paper_title: Unsolved Problems in ML Safety
problems.title: ML for Improved Forecasting in Governance
problems.summary: Developing ML systems to enhance forecasting accuracy by aggregating information from unstructured sources, considering multiple perspectives, and dynamically updating predictions to support governance decisions in uncertain situations.
problems.quote: Forecasters assign probabilities to possible events that could happen within the next few months or years (e.g., geopolitical, epidemiological, and industrial events), and are scored by their correctness and calibration. To be successful, forecasters must dynamically aggregate information from disparate unstructured sources [95]. This is challenging even for humans, but ML systems could potentially aggregate more information, be faster, be nonpartisan, consider multiple perspectives, and thus ultimately make more accurate predictions [148].

problems.paper_title: Unsolved Problems in ML Safety
problems.title: ML Systems for Identifying Crucial Considerations
problems.summary: Creating ML systems that help decision-makers identify new risks, suggest mitigation actions, and provide relevant historical context to improve judgment and reduce rash decisions during crises.
problems.quote: Separately, researchers should develop systems that identify questions worth asking and crucial factors to consider. While forecasting can refine estimates of well-defined risks, these advisory systems could help unearth new sources of risk and identify actions to mitigate risks.

problems.paper_title: Open Problems in AI Risk Modeling: Insights from a Workshop on the Technical Foundations of AI Risk Modeling
problems.title: Combining Data Sources for Risk Modeling
problems.summary: There is a need for principled methods to select and aggregate experimental, historical, and expert data sources in risk modeling.
problems.quote: principled ways of selecting and aggregating these sources of information remain an open problem.

problems.paper_title: Open Problems in AI Risk Modeling: Insights from a Workshop on the Technical Foundations of AI Risk Modeling
problems.title: Benchmark Limitations for Risk Modeling
problems.summary: Benchmarks are insufficient for risk modeling as they indicate capability existence but not likelihood or consequences of use, requiring tailored scenarios and better reporting standards.
problems.quote: Benchmark and evaluation data are widely recognized as insufficient for risk modeling purposes.

problems.paper_title: Open Problems in AI Risk Modeling: Insights from a Workshop on the Technical Foundations of AI Risk Modeling
problems.title: Historical Data Attribution Challenges
problems.summary: Historical data lacks granularity and reliable attribution of incidents to AI systems, complicating risk model calibration and backtesting.
problems.quote: Determining the extent to which a given incident can be attributed to AI systems as opposed to humans is also challenging.

problems.paper_title: Open Problems in AI Risk Modeling: Insights from a Workshop on the Technical Foundations of AI Risk Modeling
problems.title: Appropriate Structural Representation for AI Risk Models
problems.summary: There is no consensus on which formalism (e.g., fault trees, Bayesian networks) is best suited for different classes of AI risk, complicating comparisons when different architectures are used for the same scenario.
problems.quote: Each carries different assumptions about how harms unfold and how evidence is combined, and there is currently no consensus on which formalism is best suited to which class of AI risk. If multiple groups model the same risk scenario using different architectures, comparing the outputs becomes a challenge on its own.

problems.paper_title: Open Problems in AI Risk Modeling: Insights from a Workshop on the Technical Foundations of AI Risk Modeling
problems.title: Parameter Parsimony in AI Risk Models
problems.summary: Explicitly modeling parameter dependencies in risk models is underdeveloped, and the quadratic growth of pairwise correlations with parameters makes parsimony a practical necessity, though interdependencies (e.g., LLM capabilities) are often correlated.
problems.quote: A model with five parameters has ten such pairs; a model with ten parameters has forty-five. In practice, most current models simply assume parameter independence, but this assumption is rarely justified. For instance, LLM capabilities are likely highly correlated across the various steps of risk scenarios.

problems.paper_title: Open Problems in AI Risk Modeling: Insights from a Workshop on the Technical Foundations of AI Risk Modeling
problems.title: Systematic Combination of Multiple Risk Model Outputs
problems.summary: How to systematically combine outputs from multiple risk models with different assumptions or parameters, especially when they yield divergent results, remains an open question.
problems.quote: This, however, does raise further questions about how to systematically combine outputs across models and how to communicate uncertainty when different approaches yield divergent results.

problems.paper_title: Open Problems in AI Risk Modeling: Insights from a Workshop on the Technical Foundations of AI Risk Modeling
problems.title: Model Quality Evaluation Based on Intended Use
problems.summary: Clarifying how to evaluate model quality in relation to its intended use—such as setting risk thresholds versus prioritizing mitigations—is essential but unresolved.
problems.quote: Clarifying these distinctions is essential for aligning modeling approaches with decision-making needs.

problems.paper_title: Open Problems in AI Risk Modeling: Insights from a Workshop on the Technical Foundations of AI Risk Modeling
problems.title: Defining Sufficient Scenario Coverage
problems.summary: There is a need to establish objective criteria for determining what constitutes a sufficient set of risk scenarios in AI risk modeling, especially for governance requiring upper-bound or worst-case characterizations.
problems.quote: This challenge is exacerbated by the lack of objective criteria for what constitutes a "sufficient" scenario set.

problems.paper_title: Open Problems in AI Risk Modeling: Insights from a Workshop on the Technical Foundations of AI Risk Modeling
problems.title: Comprehensive Risk Universe Mapping
problems.summary: Developing methods to comprehensively map the full spectrum of potential AI risk scenarios, particularly in areas lacking historical analogues like loss-of-control scenarios, remains an unsolved challenge.
problems.quote: if the selected scenarios capture only a fraction of the total risk space, the resulting outputs may systematically underestimate the aggregate threat.

problems.paper_title: Open Problems in AI Risk Modeling: Insights from a Workshop on the Technical Foundations of AI Risk Modeling
problems.title: Granularity vs. Robustness Trade-off in AI Risk Models
problems.summary: The challenge is determining the optimal level of granularity in AI risk models, balancing theoretical fidelity from complex architectures against empirical robustness under data constraints and deep uncertainty.
problems.quote: This implies a distinct trade-off: increased model complexity may enhance theoretical fidelity, but often decreases empirical robustness, particularly under deep uncertainty.

problems.paper_title: Open Problems in AI Risk Modeling: Insights from a Workshop on the Technical Foundations of AI Risk Modeling
problems.title: Uncertainty Quantification in Sparse Data Environments
problems.summary: Developing methods to explicitly quantify uncertainty in AI risk models when data is sparse, noisy, or biased, to avoid false precision from overly granular models.
problems.quote: A recurring theme across both dimensions is the imperative to explicitly quantify uncertainty. When data quality is poor, increasing complexity can amplify epistemic noise.

problems.paper_title: Open Problems in AI Risk Modeling: Insights from a Workshop on the Technical Foundations of AI Risk Modeling
problems.title: Aggregating Weak Signals for Risk Estimation
problems.summary: Creating frameworks to aggregate diverse data sources and heterogeneous expert elicitation methods to produce order-of-magnitude risk estimates under deep uncertainty.
problems.quote: participants highlighted the utility of aggregating multiple weak signals, including diverse data sources and heterogeneous elicitation methods, to generate at least order-of-magnitude estimates.

problems.paper_title: Open Problems in AI Risk Modeling: Insights from a Workshop on the Technical Foundations of AI Risk Modeling
problems.title: Superforecasters' Ability in AI Risk Estimation
problems.summary: It is unclear whether superforecasters can accurately estimate probabilities for highly technical and novel AI risk scenarios, such as the impact of LLM capabilities on cyberattack steps.
problems.quote: The question of whether superforecasters can usefully estimate, for example, the probability that a given LLM capability translates into meaningful uplift for a specific step in a cyberattack remains open.

problems.paper_title: Open Problems in AI Risk Modeling: Insights from a Workshop on the Technical Foundations of AI Risk Modeling
problems.title: LLM-Simulated Expert Accuracy Validation
problems.summary: There is a need to demonstrate that LLM-elicited risk estimates are accurate in an absolute sense, as calibration against ground truth remains unresolved due to uncertain human baselines and sparse empirical data.
problems.quote: There is still a need, however, to demonstrate that these estimates are accurate in an absolute sense. Calibration against ground truth remains a key unresolved challenge, and the divergence between human expert groups on these topics means that even the human-elicited baseline is uncertain.

problems.paper_title: Open Problems in AI Risk Modeling: Insights from a Workshop on the Technical Foundations of AI Risk Modeling
problems.title: Epistemic Circularity in LLM-Based Risk Modeling
problems.summary: LLM-simulated experts may introduce epistemic circularity, as their outputs could reflect biases or misalignments from the same architectures being assessed, especially without robust external grounding.
problems.quote: The adoption of LLM-simulated experts introduces significant concerns regarding epistemic circularity, given that the instruments of estimation are fundamentally derived from the same architectures under assessment.

problems.paper_title: Open Problems in AI Risk Modeling: Insights from a Workshop on the Technical Foundations of AI Risk Modeling
problems.title: Credibility of LLM-Based Estimators in Policy
problems.summary: LLM-based estimators may face skepticism from policymakers despite technical performance, necessitating hybrid approaches and transparency to bridge the gap between feasibility and legitimacy.
problems.quote: While LLM-based estimators may, in some contexts, match or even exceed human performance in forecasting tasks, their outputs may be viewed with greater skepticism by policymakers and other stakeholders.

problems.paper_title: Open Problems in AI Risk Modeling: Insights from a Workshop on the Technical Foundations of AI Risk Modeling
problems.title: Methodological Gaps in LLM Elicitation for AI Risk
problems.summary: Current LLM elicitation frameworks like AutoElicit, validated for structured tasks, may not handle the ambiguity and context-dependence of AI risk nodes, requiring methodological adaptations.
problems.quote: However, important methodological gaps still exist. AutoElicit was designed and validated for structured predictive tasks such as clinical classification, and the nodes related to AI risk might be considerably more ambiguous and context-dependent.

problems.paper_title: Open Problems in AI Risk Modeling: Insights from a Workshop on the Technical Foundations of AI Risk Modeling
problems.title: Validation Standards for AI Risk Models
problems.summary: The field lacks consensus on achievable and sufficient validation standards for AI risk models, given the absence of historical catastrophic events and reliable proxy data.
problems.quote: The field, therefore, faces a difficult question about which validation standards are both achievable and sufficient to justify the use of AI risk models.

problems.paper_title: Open Problems in AI Risk Modeling: Insights from a Workshop on the Technical Foundations of AI Risk Modeling
problems.title: Internal Model Quality Metrics Development
problems.summary: There is a need to develop and refine internal model quality metrics (e.g., sensitivity analysis, Shapley value stability) as proxies for external validity in AI risk models.
problems.quote: Internal model quality metrics were proposed as a proxy for external validity in the absence of ground truth. Sensitivity analysis and Shapley value stability analysis, in particular, were noted as promising methods.

problems.paper_title: Open Problems in AI Risk Modeling: Insights from a Workshop on the Technical Foundations of AI Risk Modeling
problems.title: Partial Model Validation Techniques
problems.summary: Research is needed to design empirical studies (e.g., uplift studies, randomized controlled trials) that can partially validate specific components or assumptions of AI risk models.
problems.quote: Designing empirical studies that can partially validate model assumptions, even without end-to-end validation of the full risk space, represents a concrete and underexplored research direction.

problems.paper_title: Open Problems in AI Risk Modeling: Insights from a Workshop on the Technical Foundations of AI Risk Modeling
problems.title: Model Assumptions Tracking System
problems.summary: Developing a system to track model assumptions, their evidence, and confidence levels to monitor invalidation when new information arrives.
problems.quote: A system for tracking the assumptions underlying each model parameter, with their associated evidence and confidence levels, would allow model maintainers to monitor which assumptions are most likely to have been invalidated when new information arrives.

problems.paper_title: Open Problems in AI Risk Modeling: Insights from a Workshop on the Technical Foundations of AI Risk Modeling
problems.title: Optimal Model Update Triggers
problems.summary: Determining substantive changes in evidence that should trigger model updates, rather than relying solely on fixed calendar schedules.
problems.quote: The question of how frequently models should be updated did not reach consensus in the workshop, but participants generally agreed that updates should be triggered by substantive changes in the underlying evidence, rather than by fixed calendar schedules alone.

problems.paper_title: Open Problems in AI Risk Modeling: Insights from a Workshop on the Technical Foundations of AI Risk Modeling
problems.title: Integrating Domain Expertise with Contextual Understanding
problems.summary: The challenge is to effectively combine specialized domain knowledge with broader contextual understanding of how AI systems alter operational dynamics, as these expertise types often reside in different entities.
problems.quote: Domain expertise must be paired with contextual understanding

problems.paper_title: Open Problems in AI Risk Modeling: Insights from a Workshop on the Technical Foundations of AI Risk Modeling
problems.title: Structurally Independent Evaluation and Verification Structures
problems.summary: The need for independent evaluation and verification structures to avoid conflicts of interest, as the same organization should not both support and audit AI risk models.
problems.quote: The same organization should not both support and audit the same model

problems.paper_title: Open Problems in AI Risk Modeling: Insights from a Workshop on the Technical Foundations of AI Risk Modeling
problems.title: Division of Responsibilities Between Model Builders and Evaluators
problems.summary: Clarifying distinct roles between model providers (generating baseline risk models) and external evaluators (validating/challenging models) to ensure legitimacy in governance applications.
problems.quote: Model developers and external evaluators should play distinct roles

problems.paper_title: Open Problems in AI Risk Modeling: Insights from a Workshop on the Technical Foundations of AI Risk Modeling
problems.title: Tiered Disclosure Systems for Risk Model Information
problems.summary: Developing tiered disclosure systems to balance sharing risk model insights broadly while protecting sensitive details from misuse, depending on recipients' security clearance/legal mandates.
problems.quote: Information sharing requires tiered disclosure systems

problems.paper_title: Open Problems in AI Risk Modeling: Insights from a Workshop on the Technical Foundations of AI Risk Modeling
problems.title: Liability Protections for Early Risk Disclosure
problems.summary: Establishing safe-harbor arrangements to protect developers/evaluators from legal/reputational consequences when disclosing risks before mitigations exist, incentivizing early reporting.
problems.quote: Liability protections are needed to help incentivise disclosure

problems.paper_title: Open Problems in AI Risk Modeling: Insights from a Workshop on the Technical Foundations of AI Risk Modeling
problems.title: Designing Insulated AI Risk Assessment Body
problems.summary: The challenge is to create an overarching assessment body for AI risk that is institutionally insulated from political and commercial pressures while maintaining legitimacy through broad participation.
problems.quote: The question of how to design an overarching assessment body that is institutionally insulated from these pressures without sacrificing the legitimacy that comes from broad participation is at least as much a political design problem as a governance or technical one.

problems.paper_title: Open Problems in AI Risk Modeling: Insights from a Workshop on the Technical Foundations of AI Risk Modeling
problems.title: Developing AI Risk Monitoring and Update Systems
problems.summary: There is a need for institutions that can monitor AI systems over time, collect incident reports and usage data, and convert these into triggers for review or revision as capabilities and threats evolve.
problems.quote: Participants also emphasized the importance of monitoring systems over time, especially for updating assumptions as model capabilities, usage patterns, and threat environments change.

problems.paper_title: Open Problems in AI Risk Modeling: Insights from a Workshop on the Technical Foundations of AI Risk Modeling
problems.title: Establishing Independent AI Risk Information-Sharing Entity
problems.summary: The need exists for an independent, trusted third-party entity (like an AI ISAC) to facilitate neutral information sharing and risk intelligence repository, modeled after systems like NASA's ASRS.
problems.quote: Participants also expressed the need for an independent (non-government non-industry) trusted third party entity to facilitate information sharing.

problems.paper_title: Open Problems in AI Risk Modeling: Insights from a Workshop on the Technical Foundations of AI Risk Modeling
problems.title: Governance Model Appropriateness for Decision Contexts
problems.summary: Future institutional design work should focus on clarifying which governance arrangements are appropriate for specific decision contexts, rather than seeking a single optimal model.
problems.quote: This suggests that future institutional design work should not aim to identify a single best model of governance, but rather to clarify which arrangements are appropriate for which decision contexts.

problems.paper_title: Open Problems in AI Risk Modeling: Insights from a Workshop on the Technical Foundations of AI Risk Modeling
problems.title: Tradeoff Between Participation and Effectiveness
problems.summary: There is a tradeoff between broad participation (which increases legitimacy but complicates consensus) and specialized oversight (which improves operational effectiveness but risks reduced trust and information access).
problems.quote: Participants also noted a likely tradeoff between broad participation and operational effectiveness. A highly participatory process may increase legitimacy, but it can also make consensus harder to achieve and create opportunities for strategic pressure. By contrast, a smaller and more specialized oversight structure may be more operationally useful, but may struggle to secure trust or access to the information needed for robust assessment.

problems.paper_title: Open Problems in AI Risk Modeling: Insights from a Workshop on the Technical Foundations of AI Risk Modeling
problems.title: Evaluation Reporting Standards
problems.summary: Developing standards for evaluation reporting to ensure consistency and comparability in AI risk modeling assessments.
problems.quote: - Standards for evaluation reporting.

problems.paper_title: Open Problems in AI Risk Modeling: Insights from a Workshop on the Technical Foundations of AI Risk Modeling
problems.title: Risk Scenario-Tailored Benchmarks
problems.summary: Creating benchmarks specifically designed for particular risk scenarios rather than broad risk domains to better capture nuanced risks.
problems.quote: - Benchmarks tailored to specific risk scenarios, as opposed to just risk domains.

problems.paper_title: Open Problems in AI Risk Modeling: Insights from a Workshop on the Technical Foundations of AI Risk Modeling
problems.title: Risk Universe Coverage Assessment
problems.summary: Establishing methods to evaluate how comprehensively a model covers the risk universe and to determine whether estimates represent lower, central, or upper bounds.
problems.quote: - Methods for assessing coverage of the risk universe and for characterizing whether resulting estimates should be interpreted as lower-bound, central, or upper-bound.

problems.paper_title: Open Problems in AI Risk Modeling: Insights from a Workshop on the Technical Foundations of AI Risk Modeling
problems.title: Granularity Selection Criteria
problems.summary: Defining criteria for choosing appropriate model granularity levels that balance data sparsity and empirical robustness, avoiding unnecessary complexity.
problems.quote: - Criteria for selecting an appropriate level of granularity given data sparsity, including when increased model complexity reduces rather than improves empirical robustness.

problems.paper_title: Open Problems in AI Risk Modeling: Insights from a Workshop on the Technical Foundations of AI Risk Modeling
problems.title: Ensemble Model Aggregation Methods
problems.summary: Developing techniques to combine outputs from ensemble models, including triangulating directional signals and communicating disagreements.
problems.quote: - Aggregation methods for combining outputs across ensemble modeling approaches, includ- ing how to triangulate directional signals and communicate disagreement when models diverge.

problems.paper_title: Open Problems in AI Risk Modeling: Insights from a Workshop on the Technical Foundations of AI Risk Modeling
problems.title: Model Fidelity-Use Matching Frameworks
problems.summary: Creating frameworks to align model fidelity requirements with specific use cases, such as threshold-setting or mitigation prioritization.
problems.quote: - Frameworks for matching model fidelity requirements to intended use (e.g., threshold-setting and safety assurance vs. mitigation prioritization or exploratory analysis).

problems.paper_title: Open Problems in AI Risk Modeling: Insights from a Workshop on the Technical Foundations of AI Risk Modeling
problems.title: Superforecaster Utilization in Risk Models
problems.summary: Exploring the use of superforecasters alongside or instead of domain experts to improve risk model accuracy and calibration.
problems.quote: - Use of superforecasters instead of/in addition to domain experts.

problems.paper_title: Open Problems in AI Risk Modeling: Insights from a Workshop on the Technical Foundations of AI Risk Modeling
problems.title: LLM-Simulated Expert Validity
problems.summary: Validating the reliability of LLM-simulated experts across diverse risk domains and scenarios to assess their applicability in risk modeling.
problems.quote: - Validity of LLM-simulated experts across different risk domains and scenarios.

problems.paper_title: Open Problems in AI Risk Modeling: Insights from a Workshop on the Technical Foundations of AI Risk Modeling
problems.title: Capstick et al. Extension for AI Risks
problems.summary: Extending or validating Capstick et al.'s work on high-priority AI risk domains to improve risk prioritization frameworks.
problems.quote: - Extend or validate Capstick et al. [54] on high-priority AI risk domains.

problems.paper_title: Open Problems in AI Risk Modeling: Insights from a Workshop on the Technical Foundations of AI Risk Modeling
problems.title: Cross-Model Comparison for Risk Assessment
problems.summary: Comparing different risk models to determine their relative effectiveness and applicability in high-priority scenarios.
problems.quote: - Comparison of different models (primary importance).

problems.paper_title: Open Problems in AI Risk Modeling: Insights from a Workshop on the Technical Foundations of AI Risk Modeling
problems.title: Prompting Method Comparison for Risk Elicitation
problems.summary: Evaluating different prompting methods and tasks to optimize risk scenario elicitation from LLMs or experts.
problems.quote: - Comparison of different prompting methods and tasks (secondary importance).

problems.paper_title: Open Problems in AI Risk Modeling: Insights from a Workshop on the Technical Foundations of AI Risk Modeling
problems.title: Cross-Domain Model Quality Metrics
problems.summary: Adapting model quality standards from other domains and developing tailored metrics for AI risk models.
problems.quote: - Reviewing standards for model quality in other domains and creating a set of model quality metrics for AI risk models.

problems.paper_title: Open Problems in AI Risk Modeling: Insights from a Workshop on the Technical Foundations of AI Risk Modeling
problems.title: Partial Model Validation Experiments
problems.summary: Designing experimental protocols to validate AI risk models in cases where full validation is infeasible.
problems.quote: - Designing experiments for partial model validation.

problems.paper_title: Open Problems in AI Risk Modeling: Insights from a Workshop on the Technical Foundations of AI Risk Modeling
problems.title: Model Builder-Evaluator Responsibility Division
problems.summary: Establishing governance frameworks to separate model development and evaluation roles, including adversarial arrangements to reduce conflicts of interest.
problems.quote: - Division of responsibility between model builders and independent evaluators, including structurally adversarial arrangements and randomized assignment mechanisms to mitigate conflicts of interest [60].

problems.paper_title: Open Problems in AI Risk Modeling: Insights from a Workshop on the Technical Foundations of AI Risk Modeling
problems.title: Tiered Model Disclosure Regimes
problems.summary: Designing tiered disclosure systems that differentiate between structural and parameter-level model information based on recipient clearance.
problems.quote: - Tiered disclosure regimes that distinguish structural model information from parameter-level information and calibrate access to recipient mandate and clearance.

problems.paper_title: Open Problems in AI Risk Modeling: Insights from a Workshop on the Technical Foundations of AI Risk Modeling
problems.title: Safe-Harbor Risk Disclosure Incentives
problems.summary: Creating safe-harbor arrangements to encourage transparent risk scenario reporting before mitigation deployment.
problems.quote: - Safe-harbor arrangements to align incentives for good-faith disclosure of risk scenarios prior to mitigation deployment.

problems.paper_title: Open Problems in AI Risk Modeling: Insights from a Workshop on the Technical Foundations of AI Risk Modeling
problems.title: Overarching AI Risk Assessment Body
problems.summary: Designing an independent assessment body capable of synthesizing diverse AI risk models while resisting external pressures, inspired by the IPCC model.
problems.quote: - Design of an overarching assessment body able to synthesize across independently developed models while remaining insulated from commercial and political pressure, drawing on the IPCC analogue and its documented limitations.

problems.paper_title: Open Problems in AI Risk Modeling: Insights from a Workshop on the Technical Foundations of AI Risk Modeling
problems.title: AI Incident Data-Sharing Infrastructures
problems.summary: Establishing information-sharing systems for AI incidents, capabilities, and usage data, including ISAC-style and ASRS-style reporting channels.
problems.quote: - Information-sharing infrastructures for incident, capability, and usage data, including the case for an AI-focused ISAC and an ASRS-style trusted third-party reporting channel [63].

problems.paper_title: Open Problems in AI Incident Governance
problems.title: Standardizing AI Incident Definitions
problems.summary: Determine whether definitions of AI incidents should be standardized, particularly regarding whether potential but unrealized harm should be included, and how to distinguish between realized incidents and near misses.
problems.quote: Should definitions be standardised? Where does a realised incident end and a near miss begin, and should events with potential but unrealised harm count as incidents?

problems.paper_title: Open Problems in AI Incident Governance
problems.title: Validating AI Incident Definitions
problems.summary: Develop methods to assess the quality, usefulness, and intended impact of emerging definitions of AI incidents.
problems.quote: How to validate the quality, usefulness and the intended impact of emerging definitions?

problems.paper_title: Open Problems in AI Incident Governance
problems.title: Temporal and Scoping Boundaries of AI Incidents
problems.summary: Establish criteria for determining the start and end of an AI incident, whether recurring failures should be counted as a single or multiple incidents, and how to aggregate harm across multiple people or deployments of the same model.
problems.quote: When does a single AI incident begin and end, and when the same failure recurs, should repeat occurrences count as one incident or many? When the harm from one model is spread across many people, or across many separate deployments of that model, how should it be counted as an incident?

problems.paper_title: Open Problems in AI Incident Governance
problems.title: Mutually Exclusive and Informative Incident Taxonomies
problems.summary: Developing incident taxonomies that are both mutually exclusive and collectively exhaustive while remaining sufficiently granular to provide useful information.
problems.quote: Can incident taxonomies be made mutually exclusive and collectively exhaustive without becoming too coarse to be informative?

problems.paper_title: Open Problems in AI Incident Governance
problems.title: Technology-Resilient Incident Taxonomy Categories
problems.summary: Creating category sets for incident taxonomies that remain relevant as AI technology evolves without requiring frequent revisions that disrupt historical comparisons.
problems.quote: How can a category set be chosen so that it stays mean- ingful as the technology changes (e.g. a method- or technology-based taxonomy designed before the trans- former era would now classify most incidents as "other") without continual revision that breaks comparability over time?

problems.paper_title: Open Problems in AI Incident Governance
problems.title: Adapting Risk Taxonomies for Incident Classification
problems.summary: Determining how general AI risk taxonomies can be adapted for incident classification and resolving discrepancies between forward-looking risk categories and actual incident records.
problems.quote: Can comprehensive AI risk taxonomies not designed for incidents be adapted to incident classification, and how should the mismatch between forward-looking risk cate- gories and records of realised incidents be resolved?

problems.paper_title: Open Problems in AI Incident Governance
problems.title: Standardization of AI Incident Triaging
problems.summary: Determining whether triaging processes for AI incidents should be standardized across the AI ecosystem and identifying methods for such standardization.
problems.quote: Should the triaging processes be standardised across the AI ecosystem, and if so, how should it be standardised?

problems.paper_title: Open Problems in AI Incident Governance
problems.title: Responsibility Sharing for AI Incident Monitoring
problems.summary: Establishing mechanisms for different actors to share responsibility for monitoring AI incidents when signals are fragmented across the AI ecosystem.
problems.quote: How should different actors share responsibility for AI in- cident monitoring when incident signals are so fragmented across the AI ecosystem?

problems.paper_title: Open Problems in AI Incident Governance
problems.title: Adaptation of Automated Detection Systems
problems.summary: Ensuring automated detection systems remain current with evolving models and threats while balancing sensitivity and alert fatigue.
problems.quote: How can automated detection systems be kept up to date as models and threat vectors change rapidly over time, and how should they be calibrated to manage trade-offs between detection sensitivity and alert fatigue?

problems.paper_title: Open Problems in AI Incident Governance
problems.title: Balancing Data Needs and Privacy in Monitoring
problems.summary: Designing monitoring systems that balance comprehensive user data collection with robust privacy protections.
problems.quote: How can monitoring systems balance the need for com- prehensive user data with privacy protection?

problems.paper_title: Open Problems in AI Incident Governance
problems.title: Purposes and Information Requirements for Incident Reports
problems.summary: Determining the purposes incident reports should serve and the necessary information required to fulfill those purposes remains unresolved.
problems.quote: What purposes should incident reports serve, and what information is required as a result?

problems.paper_title: Open Problems in AI Incident Governance
problems.title: Scope of Mandatory vs. Voluntary Incident Reporting
problems.summary: Defining the scope of mandatory incident reporting and mechanisms to support voluntary reporting outside this scope is an open problem.
problems.quote: What should be the scope of mandatory incident reporting, and how should voluntary reporting be supported outside this scope?

problems.paper_title: Open Problems in AI Incident Governance
problems.title: Information Requirements Across Reporting Stages
problems.summary: How information requirements should adapt across different stages of an iterative reporting process is not yet established.
problems.quote: How should information requirements vary across stages of an iterative reporting process?

problems.paper_title: Open Problems in AI Incident Governance
problems.title: Balancing Structured and Open-Ended Reporting Formats
problems.summary: Determining how to balance structured categories with open-ended reporting in incident reports remains an unresolved challenge.
problems.quote: How should reports balance structured categories with open-ended reporting?

problems.paper_title: Open Problems in AI Incident Governance
problems.title: Balancing Categorical and Free-Text Data in Incident Datasets
problems.summary: How to balance high-dimensional categorical fields with free-text descriptions in incident datasets to enable both rich contextual detail and systematic analysis at scale.
problems.quote: How can incident datasets balance high-dimensional cat- egorical fields with free-text descriptions to enable both rich contextual detail and systematic analysis at scale?

problems.paper_title: Open Problems in AI Incident Governance
problems.title: Forecasting Indicators of Emerging AI Risks
problems.summary: How forecasting approaches can identify indicators of emerging risks, particularly for novel failure modes in AI systems.
problems.quote: How can forecasting approaches identify indicators of emerging risks, particularly for novel failure modes?

problems.paper_title: Open Problems in AI Incident Governance
problems.title: Adapting Safety-Critical Forecasting Methodologies for AI
problems.summary: What forecasting methodologies from other safety-critical domains can be adapted to AI incident governance given the specific characteristics of AI systems.
problems.quote: What forecasting methodologies from other safety-critical domains can be adapted to AI incident governance given the specific characteristics of AI systems?

problems.paper_title: LLM-Centric Agentic AI for UAV Swarms: Architecture, Enabling Technologies, and Open Problems

problems.paper_title: Open Problems in Constitutional Preference Reconstruction
problems.title: Ambiguity in Principle Composition
problems.summary: The problem involves the underspecification in written constitutions when composing principle-level votes into a single decision, as different executors (LLM judge, majority vote, priority vote, tree-based models) produce varying results due to implicit composition logic supplied by the executor.
problems.quote: Disagreement does not imply that any executor is 'wrong'; rather, it quantifies underspecification in the written constitution and the extent to which composition logic is being supplied by the executor.

problems.paper_title: Open Problems in Constitutional Preference Reconstruction
problems.title: Cross-LLM Transferability of Constitutional Principles
problems.summary: The problem addresses whether constitutional principles derived or annotated by one LLM can be reliably transferred to another LLM, given potential disagreements in principle application and response preference between models.
problems.quote: Constitutions are written in natural language and therefore appear model-agnostic, but in practice both discovery and annotation can be model-dependent.
